title: Your Agent Is a Lethal Trifecta (And What to Do About It) — Kim Maida, Keycard
talk_summary: The talk demos an overprivileged on-call agent causing PII exposure, a production database drop, a server restart, and a cost spike via static API keys. It proposes token exchange/STS plus an MCP gateway and mission-scoped policy to issue ephemeral task-scoped credentials while preserving agent capability.

takeaways.technique: Task-scoped ephemeral credentials via token exchange
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runtime exchanges a user subject token plus workload identity at a security token service for a short-lived token scoped to one tool call; the MCP server exchanges again for the downstream resource.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It creates a token exchange request asking for permission to access the MCP server for that tool call and only that tool call.

takeaways.technique: MCP gateway as policy enforcement point
takeaways.what_they_do: All tool calls are proxied through a gateway that checks the mission ID and policy before requesting a token exchange, giving central observability and rate limits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The tool calls include this mission ID and are proxied by the gateway which uses the ID to ask the security token service if this tool call fits the mission.

takeaways.technique: Hard policy denies for sensitive actions
takeaways.what_they_do: The STS refuses to issue tokens for actions policy forbids, such as querying customer PII, dropping a production database, or restarting production when the user lacks the role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: policy forbids an agent to drop a production database. A human's got to do this manually.

takeaways.what_they_do: Tokens preserve the user subject and add the agent/app identity through the delegation chain, so every request can be attributed to both the acting agent and the user it acts for.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We know the user and the agent identity all the way down the chain.

takeaways.what_they_do: The prompt proposes a mission with a goal, allowed actions, and limits; low-risk missions can be auto-approved, while higher-risk missions require user approval, and tool calls must fit the mission.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a goal of triage incident 2294 means read that ticket, summarize or escalate, but don't read other tickets and don't use other services.

takeaways.technique: Sandbox is not an authorization boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: Sandboxes limit what processes can do locally, but useful work must reach outside the sandbox, where standing credentials and external authorization still matter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sandboxes bound what the processes can do, but they don't control what is authorized to act outside the sandbox itself.
